claims.text: The as-fabricated additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a predominantly homogeneous FCC matrix.
The as-fabricated alloy lacks significant pre-existing precipitate phases.
Direct aging can form L1₂ and L2₁ precipitates in this alloy.
The distribution, size, and coherence of aging-induced L1₂ and L2₁ precipitates govern high-temperature degradation behavior.
L1₂ and L2₁ precipitates alter pathways for oxygen or other diffusing species.
L1₂ and L2₁ precipitates alter local stress distributions.
Precipitate-mediated changes in oxygen diffusion can promote protective oxide-scale formation under oxidizing conditions.
Inhibition of oxygen ingress at precipitate interfaces can produce a more uniform protective oxide scale.
Thermal exposure can cause the precipitates to coarsen and decohere.
Coarsened or decohered precipitates can act as stress concentrators and crack-initiation sites.
Precipitate-associated cracking can ultimately cause catastrophic failure.
Under reducing conditions, the precipitates can alter elemental diffusion and thereby affect phase stability and mechanical integrity.
Aged samples will exhibit a degradation rate different from that of the unaged, as-fabricated baseline.
If precipitate coarsening causes microstructural instability, aged samples will show earlier cracking or spallation during prolonged exposure.
The proposed governing mechanism applies within 650–800 °C under controlled oxidizing or reducing gas atmospheres.
Temperatures or gas compositions outside the specified boundaries may activate alternative degradation mechanisms.
The direction of the precipitate effect depends on precipitate volume fraction, size, and distribution.
